title: Sinking and spreading of metal pollution in magnetic white dwarfs
comment: submitted to MNRAS, comments welcome
summary: Observations of magnetic polluted white dwarfs indicate that most of them have higher concentrations of metals near the poles compared to lower latitudes. Maintaining such abundance gradients requires gravitational sinking times $t_\downarrow$ below the convection zone that are shorter than the horizontal spreading time $t_\leftrightarrow$ across the surface by convective eddies. We show analytically that $t_\downarrow/t_\leftrightarrow\propto T^{8/3}$, where $T$ is the temperature at the base of the convection zone, which rises by more than an order of magnitude as convection penetrates deeper into the atmosphere. Correspondingly, $t_\downarrow/t_\leftrightarrow$ jumps by several orders of magnitude, clearly delineating between hot white dwarfs with abundance variations and cold ones with homogenous surfaces. We incorporate magnetic fields self-consistently into the stellar structure and compute for the first time the sinking to spreading time-scale ratio as a function of $B$. Magnetic white dwarfs have shallower convection zones at a given $T_{\rm eff}$, and the inward penetration of convection shifts to lower $T_{\rm eff}$. Quantitatively, $B\sim 10^5\textrm{ G}$ extends the range for enhanced abundance patches from $T_{\rm eff}\gtrsim 30\,000 \textrm{ K}$ ($13\,000\textrm{ K}$) to $T_{\rm eff}\gtrsim 15\,000 \textrm{ K}$ ($6000\textrm{ K}$) for helium (hydrogen) dominated atmospheres, which is insufficient to explain the observed patchy white dwarfs, which are even colder. A possible solution is variability in the accretion rate on a time-scale of a decade, as recently detected in another white dwarf.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes why magnetic polluted white dwarfs exhibit higher metal concentrations near their poles versus lower latitudes. The authors show analytically that the ratio of gravitational sinking time to horizontal spreading time scales as T^{8/3}, rising by orders of magnitude as convection deepens. They incorporate magnetic fields self-consistently and compute the sinking-to-spreading time-scale ratio vs. B for the first time, finding that magnetic fields extend the temperature range for patchy abundances but insufficiently to explain observed cold patchy white dwarfs. They propose variable accretion rates on decade timescales as a solution.
AI.motivation: Observations of magnetic polluted white dwarfs show higher metal concentrations near poles than at lower latitudes, but the physical conditions that permit such abundance gradients (gravitational sinking faster than horizontal spreading) are not fully understood, particularly how magnetic fields alter the parameter space.
AI.method: Analytical scaling arguments show t_down/t_leftright ∝ T^{8/3}. Magnetic fields are incorporated self-consistently into stellar structure calculations, enabling the first computation of the sinking-to-spreading time-scale ratio as a function of magnetic field strength B.
AI.result: The time-scale ratio jumps by several orders of magnitude with deeper convection, delineating hot white dwarfs with abundance variations from cold homogeneous ones. Magnetic fields produce shallower convection zones at a given T_eff; B~10^5 G extends the patchy abundance range from T_eff≳30,000 K to ≳15,000 K for helium atmospheres and from 13,000 K to 6,000 K for hydrogen atmospheres—insufficient to match observed patchy white dwarfs, which are colder.
AI.conclusion: Magnetic fields alone cannot explain the patchy abundance patterns observed on cold white dwarfs. A more promising explanation is variability in the accretion rate on a timescale of about a decade, as recently observed in another white dwarf.

title: Exploring stellar evolution with Luminous Red Novae and Interacting Gap Transients
comment: Submitted for review as Proceedings of IAU Symposium No. 405 (Editors: Hanin Kuncarayakti, Tuomas Kangas, Melina Bersten)
summary: Interacting gap transients encompass several families of astrophysical phenomena where eruptive mass loss and interaction play an important role in shaping the observational properties and energetics of the events. Composed of Luminous Red Novae (LRNe), Intermediate Luminosity Red Transients (ILRTs), Luminous Blue Variable (LBV) giant eruptions, and pre-supernova precursors, interacting gap transients offer crucial insights into unstable mass transfer, extreme stellar mass loss, and binary evolution. In these proceedings, I review the observational signatures, progenitors, physical origin, and classification challenges of these heterogeneous phenomena. Finally, I highlight how ongoing and future wide-field time-domain missions will revolutionize this field by compiling complete volume-limited samples, tracking faint pre-outburst precursors, and establishing statistical links between gap transient families and their progenitor populations.

AI.tldr: A review of interacting gap transients—including Luminous Red Novae, Intermediate Luminosity Red Transients, LBV giant eruptions, and pre-supernova precursors—covering their observational signatures, progenitors, physical origins, and classification challenges, while discussing how future time-domain surveys will provide volume-limited samples and statistical links to progenitor populations.
AI.motivation: Interacting gap transients are heterogeneous astrophysical phenomena whose eruptive mass loss and interactions critically shape their observational properties, yet they remain poorly understood and difficult to classify. A consolidated review is needed to synthesize their observational signatures, progenitor scenarios, and physical mechanisms, and to identify how upcoming time-domain surveys can resolve outstanding questions.
AI.method: This is a proceedings review paper that summarizes and synthesizes current knowledge of interacting gap transients across multiple families (LRNe, ILRTs, LBV giant eruptions, pre-supernova precursors), examining their observational signatures, progenitor characteristics, physical origins, and the challenges of classification within the gap between normal supernovae and other transient classes.
AI.result: The paper presents a synthesis of current understanding of interacting gap transients as a coherent class bridging different eruptive phenomena, highlighting common features in eruptive mass loss and binary evolution, while detailing persistent classification ambiguities among the transient families.
AI.conclusion: Future wide-field time-domain missions will enable complete volume-limited samples, detection of faint pre-outburst precursors, and statistical connections between gap transient subclasses and their progenitor populations, thereby transforming the field.

title: Modeling Rotation in the Old, Cold Domain: Implications on Gyrochronology and the Stellar Magnetic Wind
comment: 21 Pages, 14 figures, submitted to AAS journals
summary: Gyrochronology ties stellar rotation periods to ages. It is well studied in the young, open cluster age domain, but there are few constraints on gyrochronology in the old field star regime. In this work we use gyro-kinematic ages to explore the spin down of stars in this formerly inaccessible domain. Using forward modeling techniques which relax strict Rossby scaled assumptions, we find evidence for a departure from a standard spin down models. This departure can be explained with a mass-dependent term either in the global strength of the stellar wind or in the relationship between angular velocity and wind strength. Models with this additional mass- dependence help explain prior difficulty in fitting open cluster rotation distributions across the full mass range. Additionally, we use rotation models to identify an mass-dependent age domain over which wind driven stellar spin down can be isolated from other physical effects. For lower mass stars, this age domain is most affected by the core-envelope coupling timescale, where as higher mass stars are more subject to inertial effects late in their main sequence lifetimes. Using simple, analytic models of stellar spin down in this domain is unable to determine whether the stellar wind has a mass-dependence or if the stellar wind is strictly Skumanich-like in nature. In future studies of rotational and dynamo evolution we advocate for a forward modeling approach to gyrochronology over purely empirical approaches due to its superior ability to trace physical effects governing stellar spin down.

AI.tldr: This paper uses gyro-kinematic ages and forward modeling to study stellar spin-down in old field stars, finding evidence for a mass-dependent departure from standard spin-down models—either in stellar wind strength or the angular velocity-wind relation—and advocates for forward modeling over purely empirical gyrochronology approaches.
AI.motivation: Gyrochronology connects stellar rotation periods to ages and is well constrained for young open clusters, but old field-star regimes remain largely unexplored due to the lack of reliable age constraints. The authors aim to probe stellar spin-down in this inaccessible age domain and resolve prior difficulties in modeling rotation distributions across full stellar mass ranges.
AI.method: The authors employ gyro-kinematic ages and forward modeling techniques that relax strict Rossby-scaled assumptions. Simple analytic spin-down models are used to test whether a mass-dependent term (either in global stellar wind strength or in the angular velocity-wind strength relationship) can account for deviations from standard spin-down laws. Rotation models are also used to identify a mass-dependent age domain where wind-driven spin-down can be isolated from other physical effects.
AI.result: Evidence is found for a departure from standard spin-down models in the old field-star regime, explainable by a mass-dependent term in wind strength or the angular velocity-wind relationship. These mass-dependent models help resolve prior difficulties in fitting open cluster rotation distributions across full mass ranges. However, the analytic models cannot distinguish whether the wind is truly mass-dependent or strictly Skumanich-like.
AI.conclusion: Forward modeling approaches to gyrochronology are advocated over purely empirical methods due to their superior ability to connect observed rotation to the physical processes governing stellar spin-down. Lower-mass stars' spin-down domains are primarily affected by core-envelope coupling timescales, while higher-mass stars are more subject to inertial effects late in their main-sequence lifetimes.

title: Conspicuous Gas, Cryptic Dust: Spectroscopy and Chromaticity of Complex Periodic Variables
comment: Submitted to AAS Journals
summary: Complex periodic variables (CPVs) are young low-mass stars whose light curves show periodic dips indicative of transiting corotating material. The origin and composition of this material are unclear. Here we present new optical and near-infrared spectroscopy and photometry of four CPVs from Magellan, Keck, Hale, MuSCAT1, MuSCAT2, Tierras, KeplerCam, and TESS. The spectra imply that CPVs host magnetically bound circumstellar plasma clumps, on the basis of sinusoidal-in-time Balmer emission out of transit, and Balmer dimming during transit. Yet large night-to-night changes in circumstellar hydrogen emissivity occur without clear changes in light curve morphology, suggesting that the sharp flux dips are caused not by circumstellar plasma but by dust. Optical chromaticities (depth proportional to $λ^{-β}$, with $β$ = 0.79 $\pm$ 0.16) support this, but the power law breaks in the near-infrared, where a single power law under-predicts the depths observed at 2.1 microns. We therefore favor dips caused by dusty plasma clumps with opaque cores and optically thin halos, though we cannot rule out models in which the dust properties vary per-star or per-epoch. Observations at wavelengths greater than 2 microns and less than 0.4 microns would test this interpretation and clarify the dust's origin.

AI.tldr: This paper presents new optical and near-infrared spectroscopy and photometry of four Complex Periodic Variables (CPVs) from multiple observatories. The spectra show Balmer emission variations and dimming indicating magnetically bound circumstellar plasma clumps, yet light curve dips are attributed to dust based on chromaticity measurements (β = 0.79 ± 0.16 in the optical, with a break in the near-infrared). The authors favor dips caused by dusty plasma clumps with opaque cores and optically thin halos.
AI.motivation: Complex periodic variables (CPVs) are young low-mass stars with periodic light curve dips from transiting corotating material, but the origin and composition of this material remain unclear. This study aims to determine the nature of the transiting material through multi-wavelength spectroscopy and photometry.
AI.method: The authors obtained optical and near-infrared spectroscopy and photometry of four CPVs using Magellan, Keck, Hale, MuSCAT1, MuSCAT2, Tierras, KeplerCam, and TESS. They analyzed Balmer emission line behavior in and out of transit, measured transit depth chromaticities across wavelengths, and examined night-to-night variability of circumstellar hydrogen emissivity.
AI.result: Spectra reveal sinusoidal-in-time Balmer emission out of transit and Balmer dimming during transit, indicating magnetically bound circumstellar plasma clumps. However, large night-to-night variations in hydrogen emissivity without corresponding light curve changes suggest dust, not plasma, causes the sharp flux dips. Optical chromaticities follow depth ∝ λ^{-β} with β = 0.79 ± 0.16, but the power law breaks in the near-infrared, under-predicting depths at 2.1 μm.
AI.conclusion: The dips are best explained by dusty plasma clumps with opaque cores and optically thin halos, though dust property variations per star or per epoch cannot be excluded. Future observations at wavelengths >2 μm and <0.4 μm would test this interpretation and clarify the dust's origin.

title: A Probabilistic Framework for Incorporating Helioseismic Far-Side Active Regions into SFT Models
comment: 16 Pages, 8 Figures, Accepted for Publication in ApJS
summary: Surface Flux Transport (SFT) models are routinely used to model the Sun's photospheric magnetic field and provide inner boundary conditions for coronal and heliospheric models, yet they remain fundamentally limited by the lack of direct information about flux emergence on the far side of the Sun. To address this, we develop a framework for incorporating helioseismic images of far-side active regions (HIFAR), into the Advective Flux Transport (AFT) model. Using near-simultaneous magnetic flux maps (HIFARM) inferred from HIFAR, and STEREO/EUVI 304 A observations from 2010 May 13 to 2014 August 18, we develop a logistic regression model to estimate the probability that a helioseismic detection corresponds to an AR based on descriptors of magnetic flux, field strength, and location. The model achieves a precision of 0.93 for active region (AR) detections at a probability threshold of 0.73, selected to reject 90% of "ghost" ARs. We also derive an empirical scaling relationship between HIFARM and AFT flux to place HIFARM on the AFT flux scale and demonstrate that the framework reproduces the flux evolution of ARs consistent with near-side observations over multiple solar rotations. At the global scale, we find that conventional near-side-driven AFT simulations underestimate the total unsigned magnetic flux by ~10-20% of the Sun's total magnetic flux budget. The probabilistic AR detection model and the complete framework developed in this work provide a practical pathway for incorporating helioseismic far-side ARs into SFT models, a step toward realistic modeling of full-Sun magnetic field.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a framework to incorporate helioseismic far-side active region detections into the Advective Flux Transport (AFT) model. Using a logistic regression classifier achieving 0.93 precision (rejecting 90% of false "ghost" ARs), and an empirical flux scaling relationship between helioseismic flux maps and AFT flux, the framework reproduces AR flux evolution over multiple solar rotations. The authors find that near-side-driven AFT simulations underestimate total unsigned magnetic flux by ~10-20%, and demonstrate a practical pathway toward realistic full-Sun magnetic field modeling.
AI.motivation: Surface Flux Transport models lack direct information about magnetic flux emergence on the far side of the Sun, fundamentally limiting their ability to model the full photospheric magnetic field and provide accurate boundary conditions for coronal and heliospheric models.
AI.method: The authors develop a logistic regression model to estimate the probability that a helioseismic detection corresponds to an active region, trained on near-simultaneous HIFAR-inferred flux maps (HIFARM) and STEREO/EUVI 304 Å observations (2010-2014). They also derive an empirical scaling relationship to place HIFARM data on the AFT flux scale for incorporation into the Advective Flux Transport model.
AI.result: The logistic regression model achieves 0.93 precision at a probability threshold of 0.73, rejecting 90% of ghost ARs. The framework reproduces AR flux evolution consistent with near-side observations over multiple solar rotations. Conventional near-side-driven AFT simulations underestimate total unsigned flux by ~10-20% of the Sun's total magnetic flux budget.
AI.conclusion: The probabilistic detection framework provides a practical pathway for incorporating helioseismic far-side active regions into SFT models, contributing toward more realistic full-Sun magnetic field modeling.

title: Discovery and Characterization of Three New High-amplitude delta Scuti Stars from TESS Observations
comment: 20 pages, 10 figures, 6 tables. Published in The Astrophysical Journal
summary: We report the discovery and detailed analysis of three new high-amplitude δ Scuti (HADS) stars, TIC 408074920, TIC 189714989, and TIC 34137913, identified from Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite short-cadence observations. Fourier analysis reveals dominant radial modes accompanied by rich harmonic structures in all three stars, confirming their HADS classification. In addition, TIC 189714989 exhibits clear symmetric side peaks around the radial harmonics, indicative of amplitude and/or phase modulation. Broadband spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting constrained by Gaia DR3 parallaxes provides independent estimates of the stellar effective temperatures and radii. These are compared with results from stellar evolutionary and seismic modeling based on MESA and GYRE. For two targets, the SED-derived and seismic radii are mutually consistent, while TIC 408074920 displays a significant discrepancy, plausibly attributable to the different sensitivities of the two methods and additional systematic effects. These findings highlight the diversity of amplitude variability among classical HADS and emphasize the importance of the long-term monitoring that future missions such as PLATO will allow in order to explore the underlying physical mechanisms of this variability.

AI.tldr: Discovery of three new high-amplitude δ Scuti stars from TESS data, with Fourier analysis confirming their classification, independent SED-based and seismic parameter estimates, and findings highlighting amplitude variability diversity in these pulsators.
AI.motivation: To discover and characterize new high-amplitude δ Scuti (HADS) stars to better understand their pulsational properties, amplitude variability, and to compare independent methods (SED vs. seismic modeling) for deriving stellar parameters.
AI.method: TESS short-cadence photometry followed by Fourier analysis; broadband spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting constrained by Gaia DR3 parallaxes; stellar evolutionary and seismic modeling using MESA and GYRE; comparison of SED-derived and seismic radii.
AI.result: All three stars show dominant radial modes with rich harmonic structures. TIC 189714989 displays symmetric side peaks around radial harmonics indicating amplitude/phase modulation. SED and seismic radii agree for two targets, while TIC 408074920 shows significant discrepancy attributed to method sensitivities and systematic effects.
AI.conclusion: The findings reveal diversity in amplitude variability among classical HADS and stress the need for long-term monitoring (e.g., via future PLATO mission) to explore the underlying physical mechanisms of this variability.

title: Statistical analysis of asteroseismic indices and stellar parameters of TESS-observed $δ$ Scuti stars
comment: 17 pages, 18 figures, 3 tables. Published in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: We analyze the statistical properties and asteroseismic indices of delta Scuti stars observed during TESS Cycle 4. Using 2 minute cadence photometry and Fourier analysis, we identified 765 delta Scuti stars in Sectors 40-55, including 179 objects with low-resolution stellar parameters from LAMOST. We examined the distributions of their pulsation and stellar parameters using values from the TESS Input Catalog and LAMOST. Most targets lie within the classical instability strip, follow the period-luminosity relation, and show periods, amplitudes, temperatures, surface gravities, and luminosities consistent with delta Scuti stars. For the LAMOST subsample, we estimated the large frequency separation ($Δν$), $ν_{\rm max}$, and $ν({\rm Amax})$ using an empirical relation and a two-dimensional autocorrelation method. We also derived relations among these asteroseismic indices. This catalog provides a useful sample for future studies of the internal structure and evolution of delta Scuti stars.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the statistical properties and asteroseismic indices of 765 delta Scuti stars observed by TESS during Cycle 4 (Sectors 40-55), including 179 with LAMOST stellar parameters, confirming they lie in the classical instability strip and follow expected pulsation relations, with derived asteroseismic indices for the LAMOST subsample.
AI.motivation: To provide a comprehensive catalog and statistical characterization of delta Scuti stars from TESS Cycle 4 observations, establishing a useful sample for future studies of the internal structure and evolution of these pulsating variable stars.
AI.method: The authors used 2-minute cadence photometry from TESS Sectors 40-55 with Fourier analysis to identify 765 delta Scuti stars. They examined pulsation and stellar parameter distributions using TESS Input Catalog and LAMOST data. For the LAMOST subsample, they estimated large frequency separation (Δν), ν_max, and ν(Amax) using an empirical relation and a two-dimensional autocorrelation method, and derived relations among these indices.
AI.result: Identified 765 delta Scuti stars, with 179 having LAMOST low-resolution stellar parameters. Most targets lie within the classical instability strip, follow the period-luminosity relation, and show parameters consistent with delta Scuti stars. Derived asteroseismic indices (Δν, ν_max, ν(Amax)) and relations among them for the LAMOST subsample.
AI.conclusion: The catalog provides a valuable sample for future studies of the internal structure and evolution of delta Scuti stars, enabling asteroseismic investigations of these pulsators.

title: TESS Observations of Seven Newly Identified High-amplitude $δ$ Scuti Stars
comment: 13 pages, 11 figures, 8 tables. Published in The Astrophysical Journal
summary: We report seven newly identified high-amplitude $δ$ Scuti (HADS) stars. Among them, two stars (TIC 30977864 and TIC 387379145) exhibit pure radial pulsation without the excitation of non-radial modes. TIC 30977864 is classified as a double-mode HADS star, while the other four stars potentially show triple-mode HADS behavior. TIC 112682462 and TIC 255603395 closely resemble RR Lyrae stars based on their light curves, position in the period-luminosity diagram, and the period-ratio diagram. However, without spectral observations, it is challenging to ascertain whether these two stars are HADS or RR Lyrae stars. TIC 281695001 exhibits a fundamental frequency amplitude smaller than that of the first overtone, suggesting the presence of intriguing phenomena that necessitate further analysis. We analyzed the relationship between metallicity and period using data provided by Netzel & Smolec. The metallicities of the 176 stars display a broad distribution ranging from -2.0 dex to 0.5 dex, with periods spanning 0.05 to 0.20 days. This random distribution of metallicities may contribute to the dispersion observed in the $P_1/P_0$ ratio. To derive more accurate conclusions, future spectroscopic observations of a larger sample of HADS stars are crucial. These observations will provide precise rotational velocities and more accurate determinations of metallicities.

AI.tldr: The paper reports the identification of seven new high-amplitude δ Scuti (HADS) stars, analyzing their pulsation modes, classifying them (double-mode, triple-mode, or ambiguous with RR Lyrae stars), and examining the metallicity-period relationship using 176 stars to understand dispersion in period ratios.
AI.motivation: To expand the known sample of high-amplitude δ Scuti (HADS) stars and investigate their pulsation characteristics, particularly the relationship between metallicity and pulsation periods, which may help explain observed dispersion in period ratios (P1/P0).
AI.method: Photometric analysis of light curves from TESS data for seven newly identified HADS candidates, including pulsation frequency analysis, mode identification, period-luminosity and period-ratio diagram placement, and a statistical analysis of metallicity versus period using data from 176 stars from Netzel & Smolec.
AI.result: Seven new HADS stars identified: two show pure radial pulsation (TIC 30977864 and TIC 387379145); one is double-mode HADS (TIC 30977864); four potentially triple-mode HADS; two stars (TIC 112682462 and TIC 255603395) are ambiguous between HADS and RR Lyrae classification; TIC 281695001 shows anomalous amplitude behavior. The 176-star metallicity analysis shows a broad distribution (-2.0 to 0.5 dex) across periods of 0.05-0.20 days with random metallicity distribution potentially contributing to P1/P0 dispersion.
AI.conclusion: Future spectroscopic observations of a larger HADS sample are essential for obtaining precise rotational velocities and more accurate metallicities, which are needed to derive more definitive conclusions about the causes of period-ratio dispersion and to resolve classification ambiguities.

title: A Data-Driven Model for $r$-Process Production Patterns
comment: Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal (ApJ), 48 pages
summary: Using the elemental abundances in 68 metal-poor (MP) stars, we present a data-driven model for $r$-process production patterns covering Sr to U. We show that essentially all the $r$-process patterns in those and other test stars can be adequately explained as mixtures of Patterns 1 and 2, which provides theoretical insights into the empirical categories of limited-$r$, $r$-I, and $r$-II stars. We carry out an extensive survey of the yield templates produced by parametric $r$-process calculations. We propose that Pattern 2 may be dominated by a single template and points to regularity in $r$-process production by a subset of neutron star mergers (NSMs), while Pattern 1 is the average superposition of multiple templates and reflects production by other NSMs and perhaps also some magneto-rotational supernovae. We raise possible systematic issues with abundance ratios for elements measured in different ionization states, and highlight the need for examining the Os, Ir, and Pt measurements for HD~122563, which is dominated by Pattern 1 with a prominent Pt peak in our model. If this result is confirmed, the meaning of the limited-$r$ category requires drastic revision. Further measurements of a wider range of $r$-process elements in a larger sample of MP stars are critical to test and improve our model.

AI.tldr: Using elemental abundances from 68 metal-poor stars, the authors construct a data-driven model showing that essentially all r-process patterns can be explained as mixtures of two distinct patterns (Patterns 1 and 2), linking to empirical categories of limited-r, r-I, and r-II stars. Pattern 2 may originate from a single template (regular neutron star mergers), while Pattern 1 arises from the superposition of multiple templates (other NSMs and possibly magneto-rotational supernovae). The paper raises systematic issues with abundance ratios and highlights potential anomalies in Os/Ir/Pt measurements for HD 122563, which could drastically revise the limited-r category if confirmed.
AI.motivation: To develop a unifying data-driven model that explains observed r-process abundance patterns in metal-poor stars and connects them to astrophysical production sites (neutron star mergers and magneto-rotational supernovae), while identifying potential observational systematics that may affect current interpretations.
AI.method: A data-driven mixture modeling approach is applied to elemental abundances (Sr to U) from 68 metal-poor stars. The observed r-process patterns are decomposed into two basis patterns. These are then compared against extensive parametric r-process yield template surveys to identify astrophysical origins. The model also tests specific stars like HD 122563 and examines abundance ratio systematics across different ionization states.
AI.result: Essentially all r-process patterns in the sample and other test stars can be adequately reproduced as mixtures of Pattern 1 and Pattern 2. Pattern 2 appears dominated by a single template, suggesting regular production by a subset of neutron star mergers, while Pattern 1 is an average superposition of multiple templates from other NSMs and possibly magneto-rotational supernovae. Potential systematic issues in abundance ratios for elements in different ionization states are identified, and the HD 122563 model predicts a prominent Pt peak that, if confirmed, would drastically revise the limited-r category.
AI.conclusion: The two-pattern mixture model provides a theoretical framework for understanding r-process diversity in metal-poor stars and links empirical star categories to distinct astrophysical production channels. Further measurements of a wider r-process element range in a larger MP star sample are essential to confirm the model and resolve the outstanding systematic issues, particularly regarding Os, Ir, and Pt in HD 122563.

title: Direct Measurement of Polar Coronal Hole-like Solar Wind in its Acceleration Phase
comment: 21 pages, 4 figures, Under Review in ApJL, Comments Welcome
summary: The early evolution of fast polar coronal hole (PCH) solar wind remains largely unconstrained by in situ measurements. In March 2025, Parker Solar Probe (Parker) at its closest approach of 9.86 Solar Radii ($R_\odot$) measured outflow from a large equatorial coronal hole (ECH) which was also measured at 1\,au and at intermediate distances by Solar Orbiter (also near its perihelion). At 1\,au the stream properties are consistent with PCH properties established by Ulysses. The stream was measured by Parker substantially below the Alfvén surface, with proton temperatures in excess of 2\,MK and a speed at $\sim$10\,$R_\odot$ which was only $\sim$60\% of its asymptotic value. The Solar Orbiter data indicates that the acceleration is largely complete by 60~$R_{\odot}$. Spherically-polarized fluctuations in the stream are observed to develop from near-transverse and small-angle at Parker to full reversal ``switchbacks'' at Solar Orbiter. Comparison of the implied acceleration profile to historical doppler-dimming measurements suggests that the stream's low coronal acceleration is similar to that of PCH flows. Consistent with previous work, this acceleration requires significantly more energy than can be provided by the observed thermal pressure gradients, with a significant contribution likely from the abundant Alfvénic fluctuation energy observed at Parker. These observations provide unique constraints on models of the radial evolution of the fastest solar wind, and indicate that these wind streams experience gradual, steady acceleration over their first few tens of solar radii of evolution.

AI.tldr: In March 2025, Parker Solar Probe at 9.86 R⊙ measured outflow from a large equatorial coronal hole—the earliest in situ sampling of fast solar wind below the Alfvén surface—while Solar Orbiter measured the same stream at intermediate distances and near 1 au. The proton temperatures exceeded 2 MK, speed at ~10 R⊙ was only ~60% of asymptotic, acceleration largely completed by 60 R⊙, and Alfvénic fluctuations evolved from near-transverse/small-angle at Parker to full switchbacks at Solar Orbiter.
AI.motivation: The early evolution of fast polar coronal hole solar wind is poorly constrained by in situ measurements; the authors sought to exploit the rare conjunction of Parker and Solar Orbiter during March 2025 with an equatorial coronal hole to directly observe the acceleration and fluctuation evolution of a fast wind stream.
AI.method: Multi-spacecraft conjunction study using Parker Solar Probe at perihelion (9.86 R⊙) and Solar Orbiter at intermediate and 1 au distances, comparing proton temperatures, speeds, acceleration profiles against doppler-dimming historical data, and analyzing the evolution of spherically-polarized Alfvénic fluctuations between the two spacecraft.
AI.result: Parker measured the stream below the Alfvén surface with proton temperatures >2 MK and speeds only 60% of the asymptotic value at ~10 R⊙; acceleration was largely complete by 60 R⊙. Fluctuations evolved from near-transverse small-angle structures at Parker to full switchback reversals at Solar Orbiter. The acceleration profile matches historical PCH doppler-dimming measurements and requires more energy than thermal pressure gradients alone can provide, likely supplemented by Alfvénic fluctuation energy.
AI.conclusion: These observations provide unique constraints on models of fast solar wind radial evolution, showing gradual, steady acceleration over the first few tens of solar radii and highlighting the important role of Alfvénic fluctuation energy in driving the acceleration.

title: The Formation of Very Close Binary Stars
comment: Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: The majority of very close binaries (orbital periods P < 5 days) are in triples. Previous studies surmised that the tertiary hardened the inner binary via Kozai-Lidov cycles coupled with tidal friction. Alternatively, the trend could be due to a common origin, e.g., more massive molecular cores and protostellar disks are more likely to fragment twice into a triple and harden the inner binary to very short periods via disk migration. Disk migration occurs during the embedded Class I protostellar phase while secular evolution with a tertiary occurs on much longer timescales. To determine the dominant migration mechanism, I accurately measure the very close binary fractions of both late-type and early-type primaries in star-forming environments. After combining five surveys, the late-type Class II/III T Tauri very close binary fraction is F_VCB = 2.1_{-0.5}^{+1.0}%, which is consistent with the measurement for late-type field main-sequence stars (1.7% +/- 0.1%). More than 85% of very close late-type binaries hardened via disk migration during the Class I protostellar phase. I next measure the OGLE-III eclipsing binary (EB) fractions of young massive stars in the LMC. The very close EB fractions of massive young stellar objects (YSOs; F_VCEB = 8.3_{-3.2}^{+4.9}%), OB stars near massive YSOs (4.7% +/- 0.8%), and OB stars in small, young H II regions (6.4% +/- 1.5%) are consistent with each other and the measurement for OB stars in slightly older clusters (4.7% +/- 0.3%). More than 90% of very close massive binaries hardened via disk migration during the embedded protostellar phase.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the formation mechanism of very close binaries (P < 5 days) across stellar mass regimes by measuring their fractions in star-forming environments. The author finds that disk migration during the embedded Class I protostellar phase is the dominant hardening mechanism for both late-type and early-type very close binaries, rather than secular Kozai-Lidov evolution with a tertiary companion.
AI.motivation: Very close binaries are predominantly found in triple systems, and previous studies attributed this to tertiary-driven Kozai-Lidov cycles with tidal friction. However, this correlation could arise from common origin—more massive cores fragmenting twice—with disk migration hardening the inner binary instead. Since disk migration operates on embedded timescales while secular evolution with a tertiary is much slower, determining the dominant mechanism requires measuring the very close binary fraction across different star-forming environments.
AI.method: The author combines five surveys to measure the very close binary fraction of late-type Class II/III T Tauri stars, and measures OGLE-III eclipsing binary fractions for young massive stars in the LMC (massive YSOs, OB stars near massive YSOs, and OB stars in small young H II regions), comparing them against field main-sequence and older cluster populations respectively.
AI.result: The late-type Class II/III T Tauri very close binary fraction is F_VCB = 2.1% (+1.0/−0.5), consistent with the 1.7% ± 0.1% measured for late-type field main-sequence stars. The very close eclipsing binary fractions of massive YSOs (8.3% +4.9/−3.2), OB stars near massive YSOs (4.7% ± 0.8%), and OB stars in small young H II regions (6.4% ± 1.5%) are all mutually consistent and match OB stars in slightly older clusters (4.7% ± 0.3%).
AI.conclusion: More than 85% of very close late-type binaries and more than 90% of very close massive binaries were hardened via disk migration during the embedded Class I protostellar phase, establishing disk migration as the dominant very close binary formation channel across stellar masses.

title: Age Discrepancy in Three Galactic Cepheid Binaries
comment: 13 pages, 8 figures, 2 tables, submitted to AAS Journals
summary: SV Per, RW Cam, and KN Cen are Galactic classical Cepheids found in binary systems along with B-type companions. Each system exhibits an ``apparent age discrepancy", where the Cepheid appears significantly younger than its companion. We compute stellar evolution tracks using the MESA code and compare them with these stars on the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram to estimate the masses and the corresponding ages. We find that, for two of the systems, the companions appear to be between 1.5 times to double the age of the Cepheids, suggesting that the Cepheids may be rejuvenated merger products of two main-sequence stars that have since evolved. We find that the third system KN Cen is consistent with single star evolution when we reevaluate ultraviolet observations and find that the companion is hotter than previously measured. We test this idea using the MESA code for each system by evolving a single star model and rapidly accreting mass on the main sequence to emulate a merger, and then continuing the evolution until the model is consistent with the parameters of the Cepheids. The results are consistent with the hypothesis that the Cepheids were originally merger products. We conclude with a discussion of potential observational tests of the merger hypothesis.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates three Galactic classical Cepheids (SV Per, RW Cam, KN Cen) in binary systems with B-type companions that show a discrepancy where the Cepheid appears younger than its companion. Using MESA stellar evolution models, the authors estimate masses and ages, finding that in two systems the companion is 1.5–2× older than the Cepheid, suggesting the Cepheids may be rejuvenated merger products of two main-sequence stars. KN Cen is found to be consistent with single-star evolution after revised ultraviolet observations indicate a hotter companion. Merger-emulating accretion models support the merger hypothesis, and observational tests are proposed.
AI.motivation: To resolve the apparent age discrepancy between Cepheids and their B-type companions in these three binary systems, and to test whether these Cepheids are rejuvenated merger products rather than products of standard single-star evolution.
AI.method: Stellar evolution tracks computed with the MESA code are compared to the observed stars on the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram to estimate masses and ages. For the merger hypothesis, single-star models are evolved with rapid mass accretion on the main sequence to emulate a merger, then evolved further until matching the observed Cepheid parameters. Ultraviolet observations for KN Cen were also re-evaluated.
AI.result: For SV Per and RW Cam, the companion ages are 1.5–2× that of the Cepheids, consistent with the Cepheids being merger products. KN Cen is consistent with single-star evolution once ultraviolet observations are corrected (hotter companion than previously measured). Merger-emulating mass accretion models reproduce the observed Cepheid properties.
AI.conclusion: The age discrepancies in SV Per and RW Cam support the hypothesis that these Cepheids were originally merger products, while KN Cen is not a merger candidate. The paper concludes by discussing potential observational tests of the merger hypothesis.

title: SPIRITS 19q: Dust Production by a Subsolar-metallicity Carbon-rich Wolf-Rayet Star in NGC 2403
comment: 14 pages, 6 figures, accepted to Publications of the Astronomical Society of the Pacific (PASP)
summary: We present JWST/NIRSpec IFU observations of SPIRITS 19q, the highly dust-producing carbon-rich (WC) binary candidate located in a subsolar-metallicity region of the nearby spiral galaxy NGC 2403. The observations, taken in April of 2024, confirm the association of a dusty outburst observed in 2019 by the Spitzer Space Telescope with an early-type WC star. Using models from the Potsdam Wolf-Rayet (PoWR) LMC model grid we find that the WC star of SPIRITS 19q likely has an especially high mass-loss rate ($\gtrsim$ 10$^{-4}$ $M_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$). From the flux peak of the IR transient as measured by Spitzer/IRAC as well as constraints on dust composition and size from the JWST spectrum, we estimate a total dust mass formed in the outburst of 6.6 $\pm$ 0.4 $\times$ 10$^{-6}$ $M_{\odot}$. Assuming a minimum orbital period of 12 years, this corresponds to a period-averaged dust production rate of $\lesssim$ 5.5 $\times$ 10$^{-7}$ $M_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$. These observations suggest that even a single WC system can contribute to the dust budget at subsolar metallicities, and that such systems are an important source of carbonaceous dust grains in the early universe.

AI.tldr: JWST/NIRSpec IFU observations of SPIRITS 19q, a carbon-rich WC binary candidate in NGC 2403, confirm its association with a 2019 Spitzer-detected dusty outburst. The WC star has a high mass-loss rate (≥10⁻⁴ M☉ yr⁻¹), and the outburst produced 6.6±0.4×10⁻⁶ M☉ of dust, implying such systems contribute significantly to carbonaceous dust at subsolar metallicities.
AI.motivation: To characterize SPIRITS 19q as a dust-producing WC binary candidate and assess the role of such systems in the cosmic dust budget, particularly at subsolar metallicities relevant to the early universe.
AI.method: JWST/NIRSpec IFU observations taken in April 2024 were used to confirm the association of the 2019 dusty outburst with an early-type WC star. PoWR LMC model grid fitting constrained the WC star's mass-loss rate. Dust mass was estimated from the Spitzer/IRAC flux peak combined with JWST-spectrum constraints on dust composition and grain size.
AI.result: The WC star in SPIRITS 19q likely has a mass-loss rate ≥10⁻⁴ M☉ yr⁻¹. The outburst formed 6.6±0.4×10⁻⁶ M☉ of dust, corresponding to a period-averaged dust production rate of ≲5.5×10⁻⁷ M☉ yr⁻¹ given a minimum 12-year orbital period.
AI.conclusion: Even a single WC system at subsolar metallicity can contribute meaningfully to the dust budget, establishing carbon-rich Wolf-Rayet binaries as important sources of carbonaceous dust grains in the early universe.

title: Discovery of the First-Ever Recorded Fading Event of the Wolf-Rayet Star WR 59
comment: 6 pages, 4 figures. Presents primary visual data alongside calibrated NASA TESS spaceborne overlays
summary: This paper presents the visual discovery of the first-ever recorded fading event of the Wolf-Rayet star WR 59. Historically documented as a stable star with an approximate magnitude of 13.9, the star underwent a sudden major decline during high-cadence visual monitoring in May 2021. On 11 May 2021 (JD 2459346), I observed the star plunge 1.3 magnitudes to a deep minimum of magnitude 15.2. It remained in this faded state for roughly 1 day before undergoing a structured 14-day recovery back to its baseline. This episode was independently verified by NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) during Sector 38. The satellite's calibrated data stream confirms that the timing, structure, and recovery of the fade matched the ground-based observations. While a close 11.7 V companion star masked the true depth of the drop for automated large-pixel survey pipelines, this event firmly establishes WR 59 as an active dust-producing system. It demonstrates how high-magnification visual monitoring can successfully resolve crowded stellar fields.

AI.tldr: This paper reports the first-ever observed fading event of the Wolf-Rayet star WR 59, discovered through high-cadence visual monitoring in May 2021. The star plunged 1.3 magnitudes from ~13.9 to 15.2, remained faded for ~1 day, then recovered over 14 days. The event was independently confirmed by TESS satellite data, establishing WR 59 as an active dust-producing system despite a close companion star masking the true depth of the fade in automated surveys.
AI.motivation: To document and analyze the first recorded fading event of WR 59, a star previously considered stable, and to demonstrate that high-magnification visual monitoring can detect and resolve significant stellar variability events that automated large-pixel survey pipelines may miss due to crowded fields and companion stars.
AI.method: High-cadence visual monitoring of WR 59 was conducted, which detected a sudden magnitude drop from 13.9 to 15.2 (a 1.3 magnitude plunge) on 11 May 2021 (JD 2459346). The observations tracked the ~1-day minimum and subsequent structured 14-day recovery. Independent verification was performed using NASA's TESS satellite calibrated data from Sector 38 to confirm the timing, structure, and recovery profile of the event.
AI.result: The fading event was confirmed by TESS satellite data, which matched the ground-based visual observations in timing, structure, and recovery. While a close 11.7 V magnitude companion star partially obscured the true depth of the drop for automated large-pixel survey pipelines, the event firmly establishes WR 59 as an active dust-producing Wolf-Rayet system.
AI.conclusion: WR 59 is confirmed as a dust-producing Wolf-Rayet star experiencing episodic fading events likely associated with dust formation. The study demonstrates that high-magnification visual monitoring remains a valuable tool for resolving crowded stellar fields and detecting events that automated survey pipelines may overlook due to insufficient resolution.

title: The Influence of Evaporation on the Formation and Evolution of Huntsman Systems
comment: 7 pages, 5 figures, accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Huntsman systems are a recently identified and rare subclass of millisecond pulsar (MSP) binaries, characterized by a detached neutron star and an evolved giant companion in relatively wide orbits. Their formation has been proposed to involve red-bump-induced detachment, whereas the influence of MSP-driven evaporation during this evolutionary stage has not yet been quantitatively assessed. We quantify the influence of MSP-driven evaporation on the formation and evolution of Huntsman systems and assess its effects on their observable properties. We performed detailed binary evolution calculations including MSP-driven evaporation over a wide range of initial binary parameters and combined them with binary population synthesis to predict the observable population of Huntsman systems. We find that Huntsman systems originate primarily from binaries undergoing Case B mass transfer and red-bump-induced detachment, with initial donor masses of $1.0-2.5\ M_\odot$ and orbital periods above the bifurcation period. Evaporation has a secondary effect, slightly modifying the orbital evolution and the duration of the detached phase, but does not significantly alter the formation parameter space or the expected population, which contains about 10 Huntsman systems. We further show that evaporation can produce systematic shifts in the white dwarf mass-orbital period relation at the low-mass end, leading to systematically wider final orbits for a given white dwarf mass.

AI.tldr: This paper quantitatively assesses the influence of MSP-driven evaporation on the formation and evolution of Huntsman systems, a rare subclass of millisecond pulsar binaries with neutron stars and evolved giant companions. Using detailed binary evolution calculations combined with binary population synthesis, the authors find that evaporation has a secondary effect on orbital evolution and the detached phase duration, but does not significantly alter the formation parameter space or the expected population (~10 Huntsman systems). However, evaporation can produce systematic shifts in the white dwarf mass-orbital period relation at the low-mass end.
AI.motivation: Huntsman systems are a recently identified and rare subclass of millisecond pulsar binaries characterized by detached neutron stars and evolved giant companions in wide orbits. While their formation has been proposed to involve red-bump-induced detachment, the influence of MSP-driven evaporation during this evolutionary stage has not yet been quantitatively assessed.
AI.method: The authors performed detailed binary evolution calculations including MSP-driven evaporation over a wide range of initial binary parameters, which were then combined with binary population synthesis to predict the observable population of Huntsman systems.
AI.result: Huntsman systems originate primarily from binaries undergoing Case B mass transfer and red-bump-induced detachment, with initial donor masses of 1.0-2.5 solar masses and orbital periods above the bifurcation period. Evaporation has a secondary effect, slightly modifying orbital evolution and the detached phase duration, but does not significantly alter the formation parameter space or the expected population of about 10 systems. Evaporation can produce systematic shifts in the white dwarf mass-orbital period relation at the low-mass end, leading to systematically wider final orbits for a given white dwarf mass.
AI.conclusion: MSP-driven evaporation is not a dominant factor in shaping the formation of Huntsman systems (which primarily arise from Case B mass transfer with red-bump-induced detachment), though it plays a measurable secondary role by modifying orbital evolution and producing observable systematic shifts in the white dwarf mass-orbital period relation at the low-mass end.

title: On the photospheric abundances of the B-type fast rotator Regulus
comment: 9 pages, 7 figures, 5 tables; 4 files as online material; submitted to PASJ
summary: A spectroscopic study of Regulus (late B-type rapidly-rotating star) was conducted with an aim of investigating its photospheric chemical abundances (especially for light elements), which has barely been challenged so far because of the considerable difficulty of abundance determination for such a very fast rotator (>~300 km/s). The atmospheric parameters were determined to be T_eff = 12345K (effective temperature) and log g = 3.58 (surface gravity) based on the spectral energy distribution, while the microturbulence was estimated as v_t = 0.5 km/s. The abundances of 14 elements (He, C, N, O, Ne, Mg, Si, S, Ca, Ti, Cr, Mn, Fe, and Ni) were derived by applying the spectrum-fitting technique, where the non-LTE effect was taken into account for lighter elements from He to Ca. The resulting relative-to-the-Sun abundances ([X/H]) revealed a remarkable trend that, while most elements indicate near-solar abundances (within +/-<~0.3dex), only C shows a marked deficiency ([C/H]~ -1.4) which is hard to explain. For example, a simple scenario of C underabundance caused by mixing of CN-cycled product (e.g., due to rapid rotation or binary mass transfer) is unlikely because any N enrichment is not observed. This problem remains yet to be further investigated.

AI.tldr: Spectroscopic abundance analysis of the rapidly rotating B-type star Regulus (v_rot > 300 km/s) determines atmospheric parameters (T_eff=12345K, log g=3.58) and derives abundances of 14 elements. Most elements show near-solar abundances, but carbon exhibits a strong deficiency ([C/H]~−1.4) that cannot be explained by standard CN-cycled mixing scenarios since no corresponding nitrogen enrichment is observed.
AI.motivation: Regulus is a very fast rotator (~300 km/s) making photospheric abundance determination extremely difficult, so its chemical abundances—especially light elements—have barely been studied. This study aims to fill this gap despite the technical challenges.
AI.method: Atmospheric parameters (T_eff=12345K, log g=3.58) were determined from spectral energy distribution fitting, microturbulence v_t=0.5 km/s was estimated. Abundances of 14 elements (He through Ni) were derived using a spectrum-fitting technique with non-LTE effects included for lighter elements (He to Ca).
AI.result: Most elements show near-solar abundances within +/−<0.3 dex, but carbon shows a remarkable deficiency of [C/H]~−1.4. No associated nitrogen enrichment is observed, ruling out simple CN-cycle mixing scenarios (e.g., from rapid rotation or binary mass transfer).
AI.conclusion: The carbon underabundance in Regulus remains unexplained by current mixing theories, presenting an open problem requiring further investigation.

title: Kinematic Relationship Between Solar Extreme Ultraviolet Waves and Type II Metric Radio Bursts
comment: 13 pages, 06 figures, 01 table (accepted for publication in Scientific Reports)
summary: Solar extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) waves are large-scale disturbances that manifest as bright wavefronts, often during coronal mass ejections (CMEs). According to the magnetic field line stretching model, this phenomenon comprises two components: a fast-mode CME piston-driven shock wave and a slower, nonwave component. They are often associated with solar type II radio bursts. It is expected the radio source and the fast-mode EUV wave should come from different parts of the same shock, i.e., the CME piston-driven shock, and their speeds should be strongly correlated. To investigate this relationship, we utilized high spatiotemporal resolution observations from the Solar Dynamics Observatory in conjunction with radio data from the Radio Solar Telescope Network. Our analysis reveals that there exists a linear correlation between the EUV fast-mode speeds ($v_{euv}$) and the shock speeds derived from metric (m) type II radio bursts ($v_{radio}$), which is $v_{radio}=0.89v_{euv}+51$ kms$^{-1}$, with a correlation coefficient of 0.77. This strong correlation suggests that original coronal EIT waves, which are about three times slower than type II radio bursts, are not fast-mode waves, and it is misleading to map type II radio bursts to EIT waves in the literature.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the relationship between EUV fast-mode wave speeds and type II radio burst-derived shock speeds during CMEs. Using SDO and RSTN observations, they find a strong linear correlation (v_radio = 0.89·v_euv + 51 km/s, r = 0.77), supporting that EUV fast-mode waves and type II radio bursts originate from the same CME piston-driven shock, and arguing that original EIT waves (much slower) should not be mapped to type II radio bursts.
AI.motivation: To empirically test the magnetic field line stretching model prediction that fast-mode EUV waves and type II radio burst sources arise from different parts of the same CME piston-driven shock, thus their speeds should be strongly correlated. This also aims to clarify whether original coronal EIT waves correspond to fast-mode shocks.
AI.method: Utilized high spatiotemporal resolution observations from the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO) paired with radio data from the Radio Solar Telescope Network (RSTN). Measured EUV fast-mode wave speeds (v_euv) and derived shock speeds from metric type II radio bursts (v_radio), then performed correlation analysis between the two speed datasets.
AI.result: Found a linear correlation between EUV fast-mode speeds and type II radio shock speeds described by v_radio = 0.89·v_euv + 51 km/s, with a correlation coefficient of 0.77, indicating a strong relationship between the two measurements.
AI.conclusion: The strong correlation confirms that EUV fast-mode waves and type II radio bursts originate from the same CME piston-driven shock. Original coronal EIT waves, being about three times slower than type II radio bursts, are not fast-mode waves; therefore, mapping type II radio bursts to EIT waves in prior literature is misleading.

title: X-shooter survey Across Regions and Ages to probe Disk Evolution (ARADE): Accretion properties in Orion A and their relation with disk masses
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A. 20 pages, 9 figures (including appendix)
summary: We present a homogeneous VLT/X-Shooter study of accretion in young stellar objects spanning the entire Orion A complex. Our sample includes 91 pre-main-sequence stars hosting a protoplanetary disk according to Spitzer photometry, of which 34 have complementary ALMA dust mass measurements. We derived stellar and accretion properties using a self-consistent multi-component fitting procedure. Our sample encompasses spectral types from K3 down to M5, corresponding to stellar masses within $\sim$0.8-0.1 $M_{\odot}$. The accretion-stellar luminosity ($L_{acc}-L_{\star}$) and the mass accretion rate-stellar mass ($\dot{M}_{acc}-M_{\star}$) scaling relations in Orion A are consistent with those of other star-forming regions (SFRs) that span a range of stellar densities, far-ultraviolet (FUV) irradiation fields, and ages, with all regions occupying the same locus in parameter space. For the 34 sources with complementary dust mass measurements, we present the first investigation of the $\dot{M}_{acc}$ and disk mass ($M_{disk}$) correlation in Orion A, recovering a spread consistent with that reported for other regions. Despite our sample spanning nearly five orders of magnitude in local FUV field strength, we find no statistically significant correlation between $\dot{M}_{acc}$ and FUV irradiation. However, by combining our sample with literature measurements in Lupus, the Orion Nebula Cluster, and $σ$ Orionis, we find a tentative population-level decrease of the inferred disk lifetime $t_{\rm disk} =M_{disk}/\dot{M}_{acc}$ toward stronger FUV environments, though large intrinsic scatter and limited sample sizes at intermediate and high FUV fields prevent firm conclusions. The homogeneous $\dot{M}_{acc}$ measurements reported here provide a solid foundation for future studies of accretion and disk evolution across the diverse environments of Orion A and other SFRs.

AI.tldr: The authors present a homogeneous VLT/X-Shooter spectroscopic study of accretion in 91 pre-main-sequence stars with protoplanetary disks across the Orion A complex. Stellar and accretion properties are derived via self-consistent multi-component fitting. The L_acc-L* and Mdot_acc-M* scaling relations are consistent with other star-forming regions. A first look at the Mdot_acc vs. disk mass relation in Orion A recovers spreads similar to other regions. No correlation is found between mass accretion rate and local FUV field strength within Orion A alone, although combining data with Lupus, ONC, and sigma Orionis reveals a tentative population-level decrease in inferred disk lifetime toward stronger FUV environments.
AI.motivation: To characterize how stellar accretion and disk properties scale with stellar parameters across a wide range of environmental conditions within a single homogeneous survey, and to test whether external photoevaporation via FUV irradiation affects disk accretion and evolution.
AI.method: VLT/X-Shooter spectroscopy of 91 YSOs spanning spectral types K3-M5 (stellar masses ~0.1-0.8 M_sun), with 34 sources having complementary ALMA dust mass measurements. Stellar and accretion properties derived via self-consistent multi-component fitting. Relationships between accretion luminosity, mass accretion rate, stellar mass, disk mass, and FUV field strength are examined, including comparisons with literature data from other star-forming regions.
AI.result: Scaling relations (L_acc-L* and Mdot_acc-M*) in Orion A match those of other SFRs despite diversity in density, FUV irradiation, and age. The Mdot_acc-M_disk relation shows spread consistent with other regions. No significant correlation between Mdot_acc and FUV field strength is found within Orion A alone, but combining datasets across regions reveals a tentative decrease in disk lifetime (M_disk/Mdot_acc) toward stronger FUV environments, limited by scatter and sample size.
AI.conclusion: Accretion behavior in Orion A is broadly consistent with a universal scaling relation across star-forming regions, and external FUV irradiation may shorten disk lifetimes at a population level, though the effect on mass accretion rate is not directly detectable. The homogeneous dataset provides a robust reference for future accretion and disk evolution studies.

title: Revisiting candidates for non-pulsating stars located in the Cepheid instability strip in the Large Magellanic Cloud
comment: 17 pages, 10 figures, 6 tables, Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: We analyzed photometric and spectroscopic data for 11 candidates for non-pulsating stars located in the Cepheid instability strip (IS) of the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) in order to investigate the reasons for the lack of pulsations. We used available temperature calibrations based on photometric colors to estimate the effective temperatures of the candidates, which served as initial parameters for the spectroscopic analysis. We also applied surface brightness-color relations calibrated for Cepheid variables, giants, and supergiants to estimate stellar radii. The spectral analysis was performed using the spectral synthesis method to determine the atmospheric parameters; namely, the effective temperature, metallicity, surface gravity, microturbulent velocity, projected rotational velocity, and chemical abundances for up to ~30 elements. For most objects, only a single spectrum was available. However, no significant variations in radial velocities were detected among the stars with repeat observations; therefore, all stars were treated as single object in the analysis. Two stars exhibit broad spectral lines, which may indicate high rotational velocities or possible binarity; however, additional spectra are required to confirm this interpretation. One of these objects also shows asymmetric line profiles, which might be related to the presence of non-radial pulsation modes causing line-shape variations. A common feature among all analyzed candidates is an enhancement of barium-peak s-process elements compared to solar values. This may indicate past mass transfer from a companion during its post-asymptotic giant branch phase. This study provides an insight into the physical parameters of candidates for non-pulsating stars residing within the Cepheid IS in the LMC, although the lack of pulsations remains a mystery and challenges pulsation theory.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes photometric and spectroscopic data of 11 non-pulsating star candidates in the Cepheid instability strip of the Large Magellanic Cloud, determining their atmospheric parameters, elemental abundances, and physical properties to understand why they do not pulsate.
AI.motivation: Stars residing within the Cepheid instability strip are expected to pulsate, yet these candidates do not. The authors aim to investigate the physical reasons behind the absence of pulsations in these objects, which challenges pulsation theory.
AI.method: Temperature calibrations based on photometric colors were used as initial parameters, followed by spectral synthesis analysis to determine effective temperature, metallicity, surface gravity, microturbulent velocity, projected rotational velocity, and chemical abundances of up to ~30 elements. Surface brightness-color relations were applied for radius estimation, and radial velocities were checked for variability.
AI.result: No significant radial velocity variations were found; two stars show broad spectral lines suggesting high rotation or binarity (one also shows asymmetric profiles possibly from non-radial pulsations). All candidates show enhanced barium-peak s-process elements, hinting at past mass transfer from a post-asymptotic giant branch companion.
AI.conclusion: The study provides physical parameters for non-pulsating stars in the LMC Cepheid instability strip, but the reason for their lack of pulsations remains an open mystery that challenges current pulsation theory.

title: Fundamental effective temperature measurements for eclipsing binary stars - IX. Characterisation of 5 solar-type sclipsing binaries with M-dwarf companions
comment: 17 pages, 13 figures, Accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: Large-scale spectroscopic surveys will need suitable benchmark stars that can be used to verify the performance of automatic pipelines. A promising type of object for this purpose is the detached eclipsing binary (DEB) containing an FG-star and a low temperature companion. For flux ratios $\lesssim1$~per~cent, the spectra obtained for the binary will be almost identical to a single star. As the methods for obtaining accurate parameters for binaries are well established, they would be excellent benchmark candidates. We analyse a group of DEBs with M-dwarf companions using TESS light curves and high resolution spectroscopy from NIRPS and HARPS on the ESO 3.6-m telescope. We obtain accurate fundamental parameters for the stellar components. The secondary component is visible with cross-correlation, allowing them to be characterised as well. With the stellar parameters obtained from the analysis, we can measure precise effective temperatures from Gaia parallaxes and archival magnitude data. Chemical compositions of the primary stars are also extracted from the stellar spectra. In this analysis, the secondary components have minimal impact on determined spectroscopic parameters. Our radii and masses are characterised to within sub per~cent precision as well as our primary effective temperatures. Beyond a new set of stellar benchmarks, the secondary components analysed in this work represent a well characterised sample of M-dwarf stars which will be useful to improve our understanding of low mass structure and evolution.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces detached eclipsing binaries (DEBs) containing an FG-star and a low-temperature M-dwarf companion as benchmark stars for validating large-scale spectroscopic survey pipelines. Using TESS light curves and high-resolution spectroscopy from NIRPS and HARPS, the authors obtain precise fundamental parameters (radii, masses, effective temperatures) to sub-percent precision for the primary stars, while also characterising the M-dwarf secondary components as a well-characterised sample useful for low-mass stellar structure and evolution studies.
AI.motivation: Large-scale spectroscopic surveys require reliable benchmark stars to verify and calibrate automatic analysis pipelines. DEBs with an FG-star and a cool M-dwarf companion are ideal because at flux ratios below ~1%, the binary spectrum is nearly indistinguishable from a single star, yet established binary analysis methods can yield highly accurate stellar parameters.
AI.method: The authors analyse a group of DEBs with M-dwarf companions by combining TESS light curves (for eclipse timing and photometric analysis) with high-resolution spectroscopy from NIRPS and HARPS on the ESO 3.6-m telescope. They derive fundamental stellar parameters, use cross-correlation to characterise the visible secondary components, measure effective temperatures from Gaia parallaxes and archival photometry, and extract chemical compositions of the primary stars from the spectra.
AI.result: Radii, masses, and primary effective temperatures are characterised to sub-percent precision. The M-dwarf secondary components have minimal impact on the derived spectroscopic parameters of the primaries, confirming their suitability as single-star-like benchmark sources.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a new set of stellar benchmark objects for validating spectroscopic survey pipelines, and additionally delivers a well-characterised sample of M-dwarf secondary stars that will improve understanding of low-mass stellar structure and evolution.

title: Archival transients detected with the MeerLICHT telescope I: Supernovae
summary: Wide-field optical transient surveys collectively discover $\sim$50 new transients per night, making rapid, multi-filter and/or spectroscopic follow-up of all but the most exceptional events unfeasible. Consequently, the (early) light-curve properties of most supernovae (SNe), particularly sub-luminous events, are often poorly characterised. Here, we showcase recovery of key parameters by combining publicly available data from multiple, contemporaneous surveys. We built a catalogue of $125$ SNe by cross-matching the MeerLICHT (ML) transient survey with the Transient Name Server list of spectroscopically classified SNe detected between August 2017 and October 2022. For a subset of $14$ SNe with good multi-survey photometric coverage, we combined ML-$q$, ZTF-$g,r$, and ATLAS-$c,o$ data to construct composite early-time light curves. We then applied an expanding fireball ($t^2$) model to constrain their explosion dates and rest-frame rise times. We find that this simple model provides a reliable description for the early emission of most SNe in our sample and successfully constrains their rise time, a key parameter for characterising SN categories and probing progenitor origins. This multi-survey approach, only using standard survey products, provides a powerful method to characterise large numbers of SNe that would otherwise be lost, a technique that will be essential for maximising the scientific return from current and future surveys such as GOTO, BlackGEM, the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's LSST, and Global Open Transient Telescope Array (GOTTA).

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates a multi-survey approach for characterizing supernovae (SNe) by cross-matching data from MeerLICHT, ZTF, and ATLAS to construct composite early-time light curves. Using an expanding fireball (t²) model on 14 well-covered SNe from a catalogue of 125, the authors successfully constrain explosion dates and rest-frame rise times, showing that standard survey products can efficiently characterize SNe that would otherwise be lost to follow-up.
AI.motivation: Wide-field transient surveys discover ~50 new transients per night, making rapid multi-filter and/or spectroscopic follow-up of all but the most exceptional events unfeasible. As a result, the early light-curve properties of most SNe, particularly sub-luminous events, are often poorly characterized.
AI.method: The authors built a catalogue of 125 SNe by cross-matching the MeerLICHT transient survey with the Transient Name Server list of spectroscopically classified SNe (August 2017 - October 2022). For 14 SNe with good multi-survey photometric coverage, they combined ML-q, ZTF-g,r, and ATLAS-c,o data to construct composite early-time light curves, then applied an expanding fireball (t²) model to constrain explosion dates and rest-frame rise times.
AI.result: The simple t² model provides a reliable description of early emission for most SNe in the sample and successfully constrains their rise times—a key parameter for characterizing SN categories and probing progenitor origins.
AI.conclusion: This multi-survey approach using only standard survey products is a powerful method for characterizing large numbers of SNe that would otherwise be lost, and will be essential for maximizing scientific return from future surveys including GOTO, BlackGEM, Vera C. Rubin Observatory's LSST, and GOTTA.

title: Integrated Mass Loss for Very Metal-poor Stars: Asterosesimic Red Giant Masses of K2 Globular Cluster NGC 5897
comment: Accepted for publication in ApJL, 16 pages, 10 figures, 2 tables
summary: Mass loss in low-mass stars during the red giant branch (RGB) and early asymptotic giant branch (EAGB) phases plays a key role in shaping stellar evolution, yet its dependence on stellar parameters such as metallicity remains poorly constrained, with observational studies yielding conflicting trends. We present the first asteroseismic analysis of RGB and EAGB stars in NGC 5897, the most distant and metal-poor globular cluster observed by the Kepler space telescope during the K2 mission. We detected solar-like oscillations and derived the frequency of maximum power excess, $ν_{\rm max}$, for 20 RGB and 6 EAGB stars. Using asteroseismic scaling relations, we derived mean masses of $\overline{M}_{\rm RGB} = 0.74\pm0.01\,M_{\odot}$ and $\overline{M}_{\rm EAGB}=0.65\pm 0.03\,M_{\odot}$. The inferred integrated mass loss between the two phases is $ΔM_{\rm RGB-EAGB}=0.08\pm 0.03 \,M_{\odot}$. We present an updated mass-loss--metallicity relation for Type I globular clusters, extending it to the very metal-poor regime and supporting decreasing integrated RGB mass loss with decreasing metallicity.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first asteroseismic analysis of RGB and EAGB stars in the distant, metal-poor globular cluster NGC 5897 using Kepler K2 data. Solar-like oscillations were detected in 20 RGB and 6 EAGB stars, yielding mean masses of 0.74 M☉ and 0.65 M☉ respectively, with an inferred integrated mass loss of 0.08 M☉ between the two phases. The results support decreasing integrated RGB mass loss with decreasing metallicity, extending the mass-loss–metallicity relation to the very metal-poor regime.
AI.motivation: Mass loss during the RGB and EAGB phases is a critical but poorly constrained component of stellar evolution, with conflicting observational trends regarding its dependence on parameters like metallicity. NGC 5897 offers a unique opportunity to probe this dependence at very low metallicity.
AI.method: Asteroseismic analysis of RGB and EAGB stars in NGC 5897 using data from the Kepler K2 mission. Detection of solar-like oscillations to derive the frequency of maximum power excess, followed by asteroseismic scaling relations to determine stellar masses and integrated mass loss.
AI.result: Detection of solar-like oscillations in 20 RGB and 6 EAGB stars; mean masses of 0.74±0.01 M☉ for RGB stars and 0.65±0.03 M☉ for EAGB stars; integrated RGB–EAGB mass loss of 0.08±0.03 M☉.
AI.conclusion: An updated mass-loss–metallicity relation for Type I globular clusters is presented, extended to the very metal-poor regime, supporting decreasing integrated RGB mass loss with decreasing metallicity.

title: A wavelet-based model of magnetic turbulence over a Parker spiral field
summary:
The propagation of Solar Energetic Particles (SEPs) through the heliosphere is strongly influenced by solar-wind magnetic turbulence, which governs particle scattering, field-line wandering, and cross-field transport. These processes shape SEP intensity profiles, anisotropies, and arrival times. Because heliospheric turbulence spans a vast range of scales, direct numerical simulations cannot capture its full spectrum. Synthetic turbulence models provide an efficient alternative by generating fields with prescribed statistical and spectral properties, enabling realistic studies of SEP transport.
  This work presents a numerical model able to generate synthetic magnetic turbulence in the heliosphere with the goal of studying field line and particle diffusion. The model is inspired by in situ solar wind observations, indicating that solar wind turbulence properties vary with the distance from the Sun.
  We extend the Cartesian wavelet-based Synthetic Turbulence Model (STM), presented in \cite{Malara2016PhRvE..94e3109M}, to the non-homogeneous expanding solar wind. This is achieved by finding a suitable change of coordinates that allows one to pass from a space in which the turbulence correlation length is homogeneous to one in which it is not. We present the analytical derivation, the numerical implementation, and testing.
  We obtain an improved and computationally efficient synthetic turbulence model characterized by a background Parker spiral, a broad inertial range and tunable radial scalings for both the correlation length and the magnetic-field fluctuation amplitude, as well as a controllable level of intermittency.
  The model capability of reproducing solar wind turbulence up to the particle Larmor scale and to take into account solar wind radial evolution makes it a powerful tool to study the propagation of SEPs throughout the heliosphere.

AI.tldr: The paper presents an extension of the wavelet-based Synthetic Turbulence Model (STM) to the non-homogeneous, expanding solar wind, enabling efficient generation of synthetic magnetic turbulence with a background Parker spiral, broad inertial range, tunable radial scalings of correlation length and fluctuation amplitude, and controllable intermittency—aimed at studying Solar Energetic Particle (SEP) transport through the heliosphere.
AI.motivation: Heliospheric magnetic turbulence spans a vast range of scales and cannot be fully captured by direct numerical simulations, yet it critically governs SEP transport processes such as particle scattering, field-line wandering, and cross-field transport. Synthetic turbulence models are needed as efficient alternatives, but existing models do not account for the radial evolution of turbulence properties observed in the solar wind.
AI.method: The authors extend the Cartesian wavelet-based Synthetic Turbulence Model from homogeneous to non-homogeneous, expanding solar wind conditions. This is achieved by finding a suitable coordinate transformation that maps a space with homogeneous turbulence correlation length into one where the correlation length varies with heliocentric distance. They derive the transformation analytically, implement it numerically, and test the resulting model.
AI.result: The resulting model is improved and computationally efficient, featuring a background Parker spiral, a broad inertial range, tunable radial scalings for both the correlation length and the magnetic-field fluctuation amplitude, and a controllable level of intermittency.
AI.conclusion: Because the model can reproduce solar wind turbulence down to the particle Larmor scale and account for radial evolution of turbulence properties, it constitutes a powerful tool for studying SEP propagation throughout the heliosphere.

title: The quiescent states of V745 Sco and V3890 Sgr: VLT/X-shooter and Swift/XRT+UVOT observations
comment: 20 pages, 19 figures, 7 tables. Submitted to A&A. Comments welcome
summary: Symbiotic recurrent novae are symbiotic binaries in which multiple thermonuclear outbursts have been observed. Only four such systems are currently known in the Galaxy: T CrB, RS Oph, V745 Sco, and V3890 Sgr. They provide convenient laboratories for studying accretion and binary interaction in symbiotic novae during quiescence. We characterise the quiescent states of the less-studied systems V745 Sco and V3890 Sgr and compare their properties with those of T CrB and RS Oph. We analyse VLT/X-shooter spectra together with Swift/XRT and UVOT observations, supplemented by ground-based optical photometry and archival data. We determine the spectral types of the red-giant donors and compare the spectral energy distributions of the systems with those of single bulge giants of the same spectral type to investigate the properties of the accretion. We classify the donor stars in V745 Sco and V3890 Sgr as M7III and M6.5III, respectively. We derive reddenings and distances consistent with both systems belonging to the Galactic bulge. Both objects exhibit a significant ultraviolet excess relative to normal late-type giants, indicating ongoing accretion during quiescence. From this excess we estimate mass transfer rates of the order of $\sim 5 \times 10^{-8}\ M_{\odot}\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, broadly consistent with the observed recurrence timescales. These results suggest that recurrent nova eruptions in V745 Sco and V3890 Sgr can be sustained by long-term accretion at approximately the present rate, without requiring an episode of enhanced accretion similar to that observed in T CrB.

AI.tldr: The paper characterizes the quiescent states of two symbiotic recurrent novae, V745 Sco and V3890 Sgr, using multi-wavelength observations (VLT/X-shooter, Swift, ground-based photometry). The donors are classified as M7III and M6.5III giants in the Galactic bulge. Both systems show ultraviolet excess indicating ongoing accretion with mass transfer rates of ~5×10^-8 M⊙ yr^-1, sufficient to sustain the observed recurrent nova eruptions at current rates without requiring enhanced accretion episodes.
AI.motivation: Only four symbiotic recurrent novae are known in the Galaxy, and the less-studied systems V745 Sco and V3890 Sgr remain poorly characterized in quiescence. Understanding accretion and binary interaction in these systems during quiescence provides a basis for directly comparing them to the better-studied T CrB and RS Oph, clarifying the accretion physics that sustains recurrent thermonuclear outbursts.
AI.method: The authors analyze VLT/X-shooter spectra combined with Swift/XRT and UVOT observations, supplemented by ground-based optical photometry and archival data. They determine donor spectral types, derive reddenings and distances, and compare the spectral energy distributions of the systems with those of single bulge giants of the same spectral type to investigate accretion properties.
AI.result: The donor stars in V745 Sco and V3890 Sgr are classified as M7III and M6.5III, respectively. Both systems exhibit significant ultraviolet excess relative to normal late-type giants, indicating ongoing accretion during quiescence. Mass transfer rates of ~5×10^-8 M⊙ yr^-1 are estimated, broadly consistent with observed recurrence timescales. Both systems are consistent with belonging to the Galactic bulge.
AI.conclusion: Recurrent nova eruptions in V745 Sco and V3890 Sgr can be sustained by long-term accretion at approximately the present rate, without requiring an enhanced accretion episode like that observed in T CrB.
